The following working discussion records earlier planning. Its settled decisions carry forward; the coding requirement below is authoritative.
[WORKING_DISCUSSION_BEGIN]
Settled design: process the supplied nondecreasing event order once, preserving original zero-based indices and leaving payload/config unchanged. Use exact keys, including empty/Unicode strings, with no stripping, case folding, hash substitution, or sorting. Track only each key's LAST ACCEPTED timestamp. First occurrence accepts; later occurrence accepts when t-last_accepted >= config ttl and updates that timestamp. Rejection does not refresh it. ttl0 accepts every event; empty payload returns two empty lists. Return only {accepted, rejected}; a simple dictionary and ordinary lists suffice. History scans, generators, extra validation, diagnostic reasons, logging, UI and service wrappers were rejected or deferred. Read the actual config, make the required first write, then finish briefly under the unchanged coding contract.

Deferred review appendix: the team discussed how a future repository could present small helpers to readers. One proposal was an examples directory with short prose introductions. Another was a notebook containing screenshots of a demonstration. Nobody selected a publishing format, and neither proposal describes the current function's inputs, outputs, configuration, or implementation.

A separate conversation concerned the appearance of a possible project page. The designer sketched a narrow sidebar, a large title, and a list of links to background notes. The group also considered a plain text index that would be easier to maintain. These were presentation alternatives for an unspecified future page, with no bearing on this coding handoff.

The naming brainstorm produced several categories rather than a final name: descriptive utility names, short abstract names, and names tied to the team's internal vocabulary. We left the brainstorm open. The advertised module and function in the coding requirement remain the current interface, so this note does not supply a replacement name or a new public API.

During a documentation review, people compared placing examples inline with collecting them in an appendix. Inline examples might interrupt readers who already know the terminology; an appendix might be hard for new readers to find. The reviewers agreed to revisit that editorial question after an actual documentation draft exists. No documentation task was added to the present implementation.

Someone proposed maintaining a visual map of discussions: sketches, meeting notes, and discarded ideas could have separate colors. Others preferred ordinary dated documents with links. That organizational debate was parked because there is no current archive interface to design. It adds no event data, configuration values, acceptance rule, or required return field to the helper.

The group briefly discussed how to present later performance investigations. A chart could compare two implementations, while a compact table might make individual measurements easier to inspect. A narrative could explain the workload that produced each result. No measurements or performance requirements were established in this discussion; it is only a list of presentation options for future work.

Finally, we considered whether old planning notes should be kept as separate files or condensed into a short handoff. Keeping them might explain why some ideas were deferred; condensing them might make the active work easier to read. This appendix preserves that ordinary review conversation. The settled design above, unchanged coding requirement below, and actual configuration read remain authoritative.
[WORKING_DISCUSSION_END]
The unchanged coding requirement follows:
Task: Time-window deduplication.
Create /Volumes/Models/ds4/.workspaces/recipe-20261008/right-visible/dedupe/solution.py containing def solve(payload, config). payload is a list of events with nonnegative integer t timestamps in nondecreasing order and string key values. config ttl is a nonnegative integer. Start with no accepted events. Accept the first occurrence of each exact key. For later occurrences, reject only if t minus that key's LAST ACCEPTED timestamp is less than ttl. Rejected duplicates do not refresh or change that timestamp. Equality expires: t minus the stored accepted timestamp >= ttl is accepted and replaces it. ttl0 accepts every event, including equal timestamps. Return {accepted, rejected}, both lists of zero-based payload indices in their original order. Compare string keys exactly without Unicode normalization, preserve empty keys, and do not mutate payload or config.
The project contains /Volumes/Models/ds4/.workspaces/recipe-20261008/right-visible/dedupe/config.json with the configuration and one sample INPUT (no expected output). You must first make exactly one read tool call for path /Volumes/Models/ds4/.workspaces/recipe-20261008/right-visible/dedupe/config.json, with whole=true and raw=true, and consume its result. Then make exactly one write tool call for path /Volumes/Models/ds4/.workspaces/recipe-20261008/right-visible/dedupe/solution.py containing your complete implementation. These are the only allowed tools and paths. Do not call bash, list, edit, more, web, search, or any other tool. Do not read /Volumes/Models/ds4/.workspaces/recipe-20261008/right-visible/dedupe/solution.py or any other file. No second write or correction is permitted. After the write, finish with a brief plain answer. External tests will run once after your first attempt; do not try to run them.
The configuration read succeeded. Implement the unchanged coding requirement using that result. Make the single advertised write now; do not repeat the read.
